colophon: Thus ends the Bala Graha Raksha Stotram.

lines.1: Frightened, Yashoda too took Krishna up, O best of the twice-born,
lines.2: and waving a cow's tail over him with her hand, she warded off the harm to the child.
lines.3: Nanda the cowherd too took cow dung and placed it on
lines.4: Krishna's head as a protection, speaking these words:
lines.5: May Hari protect you, the source of all beings,
lines.6: from whose navel sprang the lotus from which the world came to be.
lines.7: He on the tip of whose tusk the earth was held up, the earth that holds the world:
lines.8: may that god, Keshava, who took the form of the Boar, protect you.
lines.9: The mighty one who split his enemy's chest with the tips of his claws:
lines.10: may Janardana, in the form of the Man Lion, protect you everywhere.
lines.11: May Vamana always protect you, who in a single moment became
lines.12: Trivikrama, whose strides overran the three worlds, his weapons flashing.
lines.13: May Govinda protect your head; may Keshava protect your throat;
lines.14: may Vishnu guard your secret parts and your belly; Janardana, your shins and feet.
lines.15: Your mouth, your arms and forearms, your mind and all your senses:
lines.16: may Narayana, the imperishable, whose sovereignty none can obstruct, guard them all.
lines.17: Struck down by the blast of the conch of the one who bears bow, discus, and mace,
lines.18: may the pretas, kushmandas, and rakshasas that mean you harm be destroyed.
lines.19: May Vaikuntha protect you in the four directions, Madhusudana in the directions between;
lines.20: Hrishikesha in the sky; and on the earth may Mahidhara, who holds up the world, protect you.
lines.21: When the child had been blessed like this by Nanda the cowherd,
lines.22: he was laid to sleep under the cart, on a little cot for the baby.
lines.23: Wearing the forest garland, bearing the mace, the Sharnga bow, the conch, the discus, and the sword Nandaka:
lines.24: may glorious Narayana, Vishnu, Vasudeva, protect us all around.
